newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs seen fluctuating, testing ceiling.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs seen fluctuating, testing ceiling.

text.p: Seoul stocks are expected to fluctuate on Thursday as buying, inspired by falling interest rates, would alternate with sales stemming from the view that the market is near a ceiling, brokers said.

"The market is likely to move sideways. The good news is falling interest rates and the bad news is the market must be tired after Wednesday's volatile trading," said Na Min-ho, a broker at Daishin Securities. Trading volume totalled 87.93 million shares on Wednesday, the highest in the market's history. The previous high was 85.17 million on July 14, 1995.
The composite index ended 2.81 points lower at 763.25.
Yields on three-year corporate bonds, South Korea's benchmarking rates, fell to a new year low of 11.65 percent on Wednesday from 11.85 percent on Tuesday.

"But in view of yesterday's consolidation, sparked by rumours of financial troubles at Samick Construction, overall sentiment must have turned weak," said Chung Chang-shik, a broker at Dongsuh Securities.
Brokers said sentiment is now different from early this week when the market rose steadily despite the news the troubled Hanshin Construction defaulted on loan repayments.
"A short-term consolidation will begin soon. It will bring the index down to around 730," said Na of Daishin.
